title: Gap in st.number_picker
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Streamlit 1.58 introduced a gap inside `st.number_input` that lets the background through. I guess this is related to the font size (of all input widgets) going from 16px in Streamlit 1.57 to 14px in Streamlit 1.58. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st st.number_input("Number") ``` Expected Behavior (Streamlit 1.57) | Current Behavior (Streamlit 1.58) ---|--- | ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.48 - Python version: 3.11.9 - Operating System: macOS - Browser: Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15401)

This is a visual regression introduced in Streamlit 1.58. A horizontal gap (showing the page background) appears inside `st.number_input` between the input field and the step (`+`/`-`) buttons. The user correctly suspects this is tied to the input font size being reduced from 16px to 14px in 1.58.

The most likely root cause is [PR #15098 ("Adjust widget/icon sizing - Part 2")](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15098), which:
- Changed BaseWeb's `fontStyles.fontSize` from `fontSizes.md` (16px) to `fontSizes.sm` (14px) in `frontend/lib/src/theme/createBaseUiTheme.ts`, affecting all input-related typography tokens (`font300`, `font400`, etc.).
- Reduced the leading `DynamicIcon` size in `NumberInput.tsx` from `lg` to `base`.

In `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/NumberInput/styled-components.ts`, `StyledInputContainer` enforces `height: theme.sizes.minElementHeight` with `overflow: "hidden"` and `alignItems: "center"`, but the inner BaseWeb `Input` no longer fills that height now that its computed content height (14px font + `theme.spacing.sm` top/bottom padding) is smaller than `minElementHeight`. The step-button `StyledInputControl` uses `height: theme.sizes.full` (`100%`) and `backgroundColor: theme.colors.secondaryBg`, so the input area's missing pixels show through as a transparent strip on the right side around the `+`/`-` buttons. The fix likely needs the input field or its `Root` override to stretch to the full container height (e.g., `height: 100%`) or for `StyledInputContainer` to give the input a background color.

### Related Issues

- [#11569 — Unexpected visual gap in `st.number_input`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11569) (closed): A very similar prior visual-gap bug in the same widget, fixed by [PR #11576](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/11576) (which removed border-radius on the step buttons). The new regression is a different cause (font-size driven height mismatch) but the same visual symptom — worth coordinating the fix with `mayagbarnes` who owned both that fix and PR #15098.
- [#12311 — Make all widgets use the same font size](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12311): The parent enhancement that motivated the 16→14px reconciliation in widget inputs. The visual gap is a side-effect of that reconciliation work and should be addressed as part of completing it cleanly.
- [#12080 — Visual gap between dataframe border and background](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12080) (confirmed, P3): Different widget but the same family of CSS issue — an inner element's height/radius not matching its bordered container, letting the page background bleed through.
